messages:
Alex Chen: quick handoff — ongoing token-store tail latency in eu-west-1 since ~06:10 UTC. Seeing p99s spike, some customers getting regenerate timeouts. Im wrapping up my window and passing primary to Priya. full context below.

IncidentBot: PAGED #eng-oncall  token-store p99 > 450ms (alert id: 6182223333)

Alex Chen: current metrics: p50 38ms, p95 115ms, p99 ~ 610ms. regen API error rate jumped to ~3.6% in last 20m. No full outage but retries visible. Autoscaler fired twice.

Marcus Ortiz: whats been tried so far?

Alex Chen: mitigations applied:
- scaled token-store pods 3->6 in eu-west-1 (k8s)
- reverted earlier read-fanout config injected ~2h ago
- enabled hot-key prefetch at edge (flag: prefetch.hot_keys=true)
- applied org-level throttle for noisy tenant (org_9f3) at edge gateway
- temporary rate cap on bulk-regens (400rps) to preserve tail latency

Jaime Lopez: logs show repeated short spikes correlated to org_9f3 patterns. throttled them at 06:22 UTC.

Priya Singh: taking primary now. Immediate plan: verify pod health, watch GC stalls, check netstat for retransmits, and hold routing weights for 15m. If p99 > 500ms after 15m, plan B = insert small in-memory read cache for hot keys + divert a percent of traffic.

Taylor Reed: Im secondary and standing by. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/token-store-latency (follow 1->2 then 4B for targeted throttles).

OpsBot: ACTION LOG: 06:14 UTC scaled token-store to 6 replicas. 06:18 UTC enabled prefetch.hot_keys. 06:22 UTC applied throttle for org_9f3.

Priya Singh: checks so far:
- `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=token-store` -> all pods Ready
- JVM heap avg ~66% across nodes
- GC pause p99 ~80ms (not dominant)
- some network retransmits on node eu-west-1b (minor but repeated)

Marcus Ortiz: if node eu-west-1b shows retransmit pattern, we should consider cordon & replace. rotating the node could remove the noisy NIC.

Priya Singh: agree. Ill monitor 10m; if retransmits persist, schedule drain: `kubectl drain eu-west-1b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` per runbook. meanwhile bumped tcp keepalive settings on that node.

Alex Chen: customer comms note: Success team notified for affected orgs; a few customers saw regenerate timeouts and retries. CC @support-runbook.

Priya Singh: if p99 drops below 300ms within 10-15m, well lift throttles and de-escalate. if not, escalate to infra-telemetry and request regional burst capacity (reserved GPUs) as outlined in runbook section 5.

Jaime Lopez: observability tip: use dashboard \"TokenStore / Latency / eu-west-1\" to watch the hot-key hit rate. to reduce pager noise: `ops mute alert tokenstore-spike --window 30m --reason \"hands-on mitigation\"`.

IncidentBot: REMINDER  annotate incident 6182223333 when mitigation steps complete: `incident annotate 6182223333 \"scaled->6, prefetch enabled, org throttle applied\"`.

Priya Singh: handoff status: Im primary for next 30m, Taylor is secondary. Alex if you want to retake around 07:00 UTC ping here. Ill post resolution when p99 stable for 20m.

Taylor Reed: acknowledged. If we need to escalate to Dedicated oncall, Ill open a bridge and add infra-eng.

Alex Chen: checklist for whoever picks this up: 1) confirm pods Ready + zero restarts; 2) validate prefetch hit rate on dashboard; 3) check targeted org throttles; 4) prepare node drain if network retransmits persist; 5) keep Success updated on impacted customers.

Priya Singh: last update 06:36 UTC: p99 ~ 405ms (trending down), error rate ~1.3%. keeping throttles for now, will update at 06:50 UTC or earlier. adding timeline to ticket.

OpsBot: RUNBOOK VERSION v2.1.2. node drain command: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. monitor rebalance before removing throttles.

Alex Chen: thanks team, handing off my shift. Priya, ping if you need anything; otherwise Ill review the incident summary after resolution.
